rows.headline: Bangladesh-India relations face strain over water treaty and transit corridors
rows.hook: Renewed political tensions threaten regional trade routes
rows.summary: Tensions between India and Bangladesh have escalated amid rising anti-India rhetoric in Dhaka, focusing on the upcoming expiration of the 1996 Ganga Water Sharing Treaty. Bangladesh leaders have threatened to block Indian transit facilities unless water-sharing demands are met, while opposition groups are challenging a Japanese-backed connectivity project linking India's Northeast. Economic instability in Bangladesh and the political asylum of former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina in India are compounding bilateral friction. Indian retail investors should monitor these developments as prolonged diplomatic strain could impact cross-border trade, logistics, and regional infrastructure projects.
rows.whats_next: Expiry and renegotiation of the 1996 Ganga Water Sharing Treaty
rows.why_it_matters: Bilateral trade and Northeast connectivity projects face political risks.
